findings.explanation: 14 ambiguous cases (35% of the ambiguous suite) repeat an identical template asking 'How do I configure/manage/set up <resource> in Terraform?' and claiming operational ambiguity between resource creation and data source query. In Terraform conventions and standard developer intent, 'configuring' or 'setting up' a resource unambiguously denotes resource provisioning (data sources only query existing infrastructure). This violates the brief instruction to 'Reject excessive explicit schema-path prompts and repeated templates even when paths are correct' and 'reject unnecessary clarification when task wording already determines it'.
findings.recommendation: Diversify ambiguous cases and eliminate repetitive templates. For cases intended to test resource vs data source ambiguity, use neutral phrasing (such as 'How do I reference or attach an existing DNS zone vs declare a new one?'). Replace multiple redundant resource-vs-data-source cases with authentic architectural ambiguities (e.g. mutually exclusive listener protocols, conflicting routing options, or distinct authentication models).
source_evidence: brief.md line 5: 'Avoid filling the suite with explicit schema-path requests or repeating one template.'
brief.md line 7: 'reject unnecessary clarification when task wording already determines it.'
candidate.json cases amb-001 through amb-013 and amb-015: identical pattern where 'How do I configure/manage/set up X' is forced into clarification between resource creation and data source reading.

findings.explanation: Cases amb-027 ('How do I set IP reputation filtering on an HTTP load balancer?') and amb-028 ('Where do I configure Threat Mesh settings on an HTTP load balancer?') force clarification between enabling the feature (enable_ip_reputation, enable_threat_mesh) and disabling it (disable_ip_reputation, disable_threat_mesh). Requesting how to 'set' or 'configure' a capability carries affirmative intent to use the capability; routing to a disable block represents an artificial ambiguity that violates the instruction to reject unnecessary clarification when task wording already determines intent.
findings.recommendation: Reframe prompts in amb-027 and amb-028 to query the status toggle neutrally (e.g. 'Where do I toggle IP reputation filtering between enabled and disabled on an HTTP load balancer?') so both branches are genuinely plausible, or replace with genuine multi-option schema choices.
